title: If there is no nominee
description: An account, deposit or policy has no nominee, or the nominee has also died.
opening: A nominee is the person named to receive the money. When no one was named, the bank or insurer asks for other papers instead.

official.text: When there is a nominee, the bank pays the nominee. The nominee receives the money as a trustee of the legal heirs, which means they hold it for the heirs.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 8(iii): nominee or survivor receives payment "as a trustee of the legal heirs of the deceased depositor(s)".

official.text: When there is no nominee and no surviving joint holder, banks use a simpler process for smaller amounts. The limit is 15 lakh rupees at most banks, and 5 lakh rupees at a co-operative bank.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 7(h) and 10: threshold "₹5 lakh in case of a co-operative bank and ₹15 lakh in case of any other bank".

official.text: Below that limit, the bank asks for its claim form, the death certificate, an identity document, a letter of indemnity, and either a legal heir certificate or a declaration from an independent person.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 10(a): claim form, death certificate, OVD, bond of indemnity, and a Legal Heir Certificate or a declaration (Annex I-E) by an independent person.

official.text: Above that limit, the bank may ask for a succession certificate, a legal heir certificate, or a sworn affidavit, and may also ask for a surety.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 10(b): Succession Certificate, or legal heir certificate, or affidavit sworn before a Notary or Magistrate; "may also call for a bond of surety".

official.text: The bank should settle the claim within 15 calendar days of getting all the papers it needs.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 31: "within a period not exceeding 15 calendar days from the date of receipt of all the required documents".

official.text: Banks must put their claim forms, the list of papers and the steps on their website.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 28: forms on the bank's website; the bank shall display the list of documents and the procedure.

official.text: For life insurance with no nominee, the insurer asks for legal proof of who is entitled to the money, as well as the usual claim papers.
official.confirms: IRDAI policyholder page: documents include "Legal evidence of title, if the policy is not assigned or nominated".

suggestions: Ask the bank or insurer for its claim form and list of papers. Your checklist links to each bank's own page.
If the nominee has also died, tell the bank or insurer and ask in writing what they need from you.
lawyer: More than one person claims the money, or the heirs do not agree.
The amount is above the bank's limit and you are asked for a succession certificate.
One of the heirs is a child under 18.
There is money or property in more than one state.
sourceNeeded: What happens when the nominee has also died. The RBI directions we read do not say.
